blocks.x: Vítor Matos praised his Swansea side for overcoming a lack of training as they strengthened their position at the top of the Championship with a 2-1 comeback win over Norwich. Second-half goals from Moussa Yeo and the Republic of Ireland striker Adam Idah wiped out Jacob Wright’s strike just before the half-hour mark.

It was the third time Swansea had come from behind this season to win, and, after West Ham’s draw the previous night, it gave them top spot in the table. Idah, though, limped out of the action and could be a doubt for Tuesday’s visit to Millwall.

“I’m really happy with the boys,” said Matos. “Players had been flying around because of the international break, joining on the last days of training as well before the game. It’s not the easiest way to prepare. It’s all about trying to reconnect everyone.”
It was a fourth defeat in a row in all competitions for Norwich, who have now conceded 19 goals in nine league matches.

Middlesbrough celebrated their 150th anniversary game in style as Will Lankshear’s second-half header secured a 1-0 victory over Wolves at the Riverside Stadium. A sold-out crowd helped mark the occasion, and Lankshear’s header from Tommy Conway’s cross ensured the home fans went home happy. The win enabled Middlesbrough to climb above West Ham into second spot. Wolves were second best as they suffered a second league defeat since their relegation last season.

blocks.c: A tifo marks Middlesbrough’s 150th anniversary before their win over Wolves at the Riverside

blocks.x: West Brom’s head coach, James Morrison, defended Nat Phillips as a “strong character” after a second successive derby mistake led to the only goal in a 1-0 defeat to Birmingham at The Hawthorns. Phillips gave away the 41st-minute penalty when he fouled August Priske, who slotted home from the spot. The former Liverpool defender’s back pass let in Fer López to win the Black Country derby for Wolves last time out, but Morrison said: “I understand he’s made two errors but it was just a misjudgement.”
League One: Plymouth on top; dream start for Savage

Plymouth came from behind to beat Wimbledon 2-1 with a stoppage-time goal from substitute Xavier Amaechi which put them clear at the top of League One. Jayden Stockley had put the Dons ahead in the 16th minute, with Caleb Watts equalising ahead of the break. It looked like the points would be shared before Amaechi swept the ball home in the fifth minute of added time.

New Peterborough manager Robbie Savage had a dream start with a 3-1 win at Leicester, to pile more pressure on Foxes’ manager Russell Martin. Posh took an early lead through Owura Edwards and Harry Leonard before an own goal from Warren O’Hora made it 3-0 just before the break. Emil Riis scored a second-half consolation for the hosts.

Mark Harris and Cameron Brannagan scored as high-flying Oxford secured a 2-1 win over Notts County at Meadow Lane. Bradford were held to a goalless draw by Leyton Orient at Valley Parade, slipping two points behind Plymouth.

Huddersfield missed the chance to go second after Sheffield Wednesday fought back with two late goals to snatch a 2-2 draw at the Accu Stadium after Jamal Lowe scored a penalty deep into stoppage-time. Kyle Wootton scored twice as Stockport came from behind to beat Barnsley 3-1 at Edgeley Park to sit third.

Gassan Ahadme’s late goal gave fifth-placed Cambridge a 1-0 win over 10-man Blackpool at the Abbey Stadium, where there had been a 15 minute delay to kick-off because of issues affecting supporters entering the ground.

Reading are sixth after a 5-1 away win at strugglers MK Dons while Luton were comprehensive victors at Wycombe with a dominant 4-1 display to spoil a day of celebration for Tom Hounsell. Efforts from Kasey Palmer, Nahki Wells, Jamie Donley and Devante Cole were more than enough against a home side who announced Hounsell as permanent head coach before the game.

Leon Ayinde’s first EFL goal was enough to move Doncaster out of the bottom four with a 1-0 home win over Burton. Mansfield edged home 2-1 in their first ever game against Bromley to halt a run of four games without a victory. Wigan remain adrift at the bottom of the table after a 1-0 defeat at Stevenage.

Burnley’s first win of the season, and their first away from home since February, sent Watford fans into open revolt as the Clarets cruised home 4-0 at Vicarage Road. While Alessio Dionisi’s fifth defeat in six games increased the pressure on the Hornets head coach, counterpart Nicky Hayen’s first victory lifted Burnley off the bottom.

blocks.c: Swansea's Adam Idah heads a goal while being challenged by a Norwich defender

blocks.x: Three goals in the space of 12 first-half minutes put the visitors out of sight and extended the Hornets’ wretched defensive record to 29 weeks without a clean sheet. When Stoke won 2-1 at Vicarage Road last month, it ended 251 days without a win on the road for the Potters. Here, Watford extended more charity to the Clarets, who ended 241 days without an away win comfortably.

Asked about the furious reaction of fans, and the rising tide of opinion on social media that his job was at risk, Dionisi said: “In football it’s normal. It’s probably better to say only one thing – I’m sorry for this match. I’m very angry because after 30 minutes the match was finished, it was impossible to come back. But I believe in my team and I believe in my job. I’m here and we work every to improve: now it is important to work well, to work better.”

Dionisi’s decision to take off popular Spaniard Iker Bravo after just 35 minutes was roundly booed, and he admitted: “Iker is a good player and, for me, he must play every match, but I had to change something and it was impossible to change everyone.”

Referee Tom Reeves did not give a foul after the Wrexham loanee raced out of his box to halt Japanese winger Yu Hirakawa in the 15th minute. By that stage the Addicks already had a lead through Karlan Grant’s smart finish but Scott Twine’s penalty in the 27th minute put City back on level terms after Conor Coventry brought down Dom Ballard.

Patrick Bamford scored twice to help Sheffield United to a comfortable 3-0 victory over Lincoln. The result, with Tahith Chong also on the scoresheet, ended a three-match losing run for Chris Wilder’s men in all competitions against a side which had won three of their previous four away matches.
League Two: Grant strikes twice to keep Salford top

Jorge Grant’s late double sealed a 2-0 win for Salford at 10-man Cheltenham to keep them top of the table. The result extends the Ammies’ winning run in League Two to four and it was also their first victory at Cheltenham.

Kabongo Tshimanga’s stoppage-time strike sealed an impressive 3-1 come-from-behind victory for Barnet at Bristol Rovers. Rovers’ record home winning streak came to an end after a two-on-one counter-attack resulted in Tshimanga tucking home under Brad Young to seal all three points.

Crewe kept up the pace with a 1-0 away win over Swindon, who suffered a fourth defeat in five league games. Gillingham moved into fourth spot after a 4-1 win at Rotherham and Port Vale climbed out of the bottom two after a 1-0 win over Grimsby.

Lamine Cissé and Ben Wilmot were on target as 10-man Stoke extended their unbeaten league run to six games with a 2-1 win over Bolton. Mark Robins’ in-form side played for 70 minutes without Maksym Talovierov after the defender’s dismissal for bringing down Kyliane Dong. However, the Potters shrugged off the disadvantage to gain a first win in Bolton since October 1990. Their fifth win in six games lifted them up to fourth while Bolton dropped to 17th.

Blackburn made it back-to-back home wins with a battling 2-1 victory over Cardiff. Andri Gudjohnsen gave Rovers the lead with a composed finish just before the half hour and Todd Cantwell doubled the advantage 10 minutes later with a shot that Bluebirds goalkeeper Nathan Trott will be disappointed not to have saved. The visitors struck just after the break through Callum Robinson’s first of the campaign.

Camiel Neghli ensured it was a baptism of fire for the new Preston manager, Graham Alexander, as his late strike sealed a 1-0 win for Millwall at Deepdale. It was coolness personified from the Dutch-born Algerian, who slotted Luke Cundle’s cut-back into the far corner for what turned out to be a 79th-minute winner.
